{{Short description|Every positive integer is a sum of at most n+2 centered n-gonal numbers}}
In [[additive number theory]], the '''centered polygonal number theorem''' states that every positive integer is a sum of at most {{mvar|n+2}} [[Centered polygonal number|centered {{mvar|n}}-gonal number]]s.

==History==
In 1850, [[Sir Frederick Pollock, 1st Baronet|Sir Frederick Pollock]] conjectured that every positive integer is the sum of at most 11 centered nonagonal numbers.
This conjecture was confirmed as true by Miroslav Kureš in 2023.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kureš |first=Miroslav |date=2023-10-27 |title=A Proof of Pollock's Conjecture on Centered Nonagonal Numbers |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00283-023-10307-0 |journal=The Mathematical Intelligencer |volume=46 |issue=3 |pages=234–235 |language=en |doi=10.1007/s00283-023-10307-0 |issn=0343-6993|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The result was generalized to the above theorem by Benjamin Lee Warren and Miroslav Kureš in 2025.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Warren |first1=Benjamin Lee |last2=Kureš |first2=Miroslav |date=2025-06-09 |title=Every Positive Integer Is a Sum of at most n+2 Centered n-gonal Numbers |url=https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/ms-2025-0037/html |journal=Mathematica Slovaca |volume=75 |issue=3 |pages=515–524 |language=en |doi=10.1515/ms-2025-0037 |issn=0139-9918|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Examples==
The first few [[centered nonagonal number]]s are
<math>
1, 10, 28, 55, 91, 136, 190, 253, 325, \dots . 
</math>
The number 47 can be expressed as a sum of 11 these numbers by two ways:

<math>
47 = 28 + 10 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1; 
</math>

<math>
47 = 10 + 10 +10 +10 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1.
</math>

There is no other way to express the number 47 as a sum of 11 or fewer summands that are centered nonagonal numbers.

Of course, the number of summands can be lower than 11. Note that the number 480 is the following sum:

<math>
480 = 253 + 136 + 91.
</math>

Analogously, here too, there is no other way to express the number 480 as a sum of 11 or fewer summands that are centered nonagonal numbers.
